mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25% per month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when the trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when the trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained industrial production contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and inflation, which erodes real purchasing power and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 12-month MA and CPIAUCSL > 12-month MA in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month MAs concurrently.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals strengthening residential demand, which boosts construction-related equities and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of sustained above-average housing starts.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) within the same month indicates a statistical artifact or data anomaly rather than genuine labor market strength, which historically precedes short-term equity volatility and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS and UNRATE move in the same direction within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in Real Personal Income (proxied by RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals weakening household purchasing power, which reduces consumer spending and corporate revenues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month MA for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is persistently below its 12-month moving average for three months.
